Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes MonoCal, a label-free method to calibrate both the scale and shape of per-pixel uncertainty in self-supervised monocular depth networks, outperforming ground-truth rescaling on KITTI.
AI.motivation: Per-pixel uncertainty in self-supervised monocular depth is typically evaluated only by error ranking, which ignores whether uncertainty magnitudes match actual depth errors across pixels and ranges.
AI.method: MonoCal calibrates uncertainty scale without retraining by multiplying by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, and calibrates shape by retraining uncertainty to predict depth disagreement with a second self-supervised network.
AI.result: On KITTI, existing uncertainty estimates are scale-miscalibrated (e.g., MonoProb error is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty), whereas MonoCal's stereo-based scale constant matches ground-truth fitting and its full calibration outperforms ground-truth rescaling across uncertainty levels and depth ranges.
AI.conclusion: Stereo-pair scaling and cross-network disagreement enable accurate, label-free uncertainty calibration for single-image depth inference.

title: Ref-MIL: Plug-and-Play Posterior Refinement for Multiple Instance Learning in QSM-Based Brain Disease Classification
summary: Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) is a novel quantitative MRI contrast for studying tissue susceptibility changes in brain disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple sclerosis (MS). However, small cohorts and the lack of local annotations make developing deep learning models for QSM-based diagnosis challenging. In this work, we propose PoRef-MIL, a weakly supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework combining iterative slice relabeling and network retraining with a plug-and-play posterior refinement module (PRM). During training, a 2D dual-branch diagnosis network and a subject-level classifier were alternately trained for five rounds. The classifier was used to update slice pseudo-labels for retraining the diagnosis network. The PRM was applied during inference to refine slice probabilities through bidirectional posterior inference and calculate entropy-derived confidence from the refined probabilities, which was then used in sliding-window scoring to obtain subject-level predictions. PoRef-MIL was evaluated on an in-house PD cohort of 287 participants and a public MS cohort of 150 participants. Compared with eight classification methods, PoRef-MIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.942 and 0.872, and accuracies of 0.926 and 0.833, for PD and MS classification, respectively. Ablation experiments were conducted to validate the effectiveness of iterative relabeling and PRM, and the plug-and-play feature of the proposed PRM was also evaluated using four state-of-the-art MIL models. Overall, PoRef-MIL offers a promising approach to QSM-based disease classification in small cohorts without manual slice annotations.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes PoRef-MIL, a weakly supervised multiple instance learning framework with iterative slice relabeling and a plug-and-play posterior refinement module for QSM-based brain disease classification.
AI.motivation: Developing deep learning models for Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) MRI diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple sclerosis (MS) is hindered by small cohorts and missing local slice annotations.
AI.method: PoRef-MIL alternates training a 2D dual-branch diagnosis network and a subject-level classifier for five rounds to update slice pseudo-labels, then applies a plug-and-play Posterior Refinement Module (PRM) at inference using bidirectional posterior inference and entropy-derived confidence in sliding-window scoring.
AI.result: Evaluated on an in-house PD cohort (287 participants) and a public MS cohort (150 participants), PoRef-MIL outperforms eight baselines with mean AUROCs of 0.942 (PD) and 0.872 (MS) and accuracies of 0.926 and 0.833, while PRM also improves four existing MIL models.
AI.conclusion: Iterative pseudo-label refinement paired with bidirectional posterior inference enables accurate QSM-based brain disease diagnosis in small cohorts without slice-level labels.

title: Incremental Learning of Vision-Language Models via Task Subspace Projection and Dynamic LoRA
comment: Pre-peer-review version of an article accepted for publication in the International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV)
summary: Recent pre-trained vision-language models often encounter a Multi-Domain Task-Incremental Learning (MTIL) scenario in practice, where a set of classes of multi-modal tasks arrive incrementally. Due to privacy concerns and memory constraints, MTIL with pre-trained models encounters forgetting of knowledge from old tasks, degradation of zero-shot transfer capability, and underfitting of new-task knowledge. To overcome these challenges, previous MTIL methods attempt to learn a discriminative cross-task identification (CTI) module and an effective new-task adaptation (NTA) module. However, current CTI modules suffer from severe task confusion between seen and unseen tasks, and NTA modules cannot adaptively balance the performance and parameter cost while incorporating task-specific knowledge. To alleviate the above dilemmas, we propose an effective and efficient TSP-DLoRA method for MTIL, which consists of Task Subspace Projection (TSP) and Dynamic Low Rank Adapter (DLoRA) modules. Specifically, our TSP module includes a task identifier classifier based on task-specific subspaces and a feature projection strategy that can determine the identifier associated with samples from both seen and unseen tasks. Our DLoRA improves the knowledge adaptation from new tasks by dynamically assigning Low Rank Adapter (LoRA) across transformer layers based on the task distributions. Experimental evaluations across 11 datasets, using three performance metrics, demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes TSP-DLoRA for Multi-Domain Task-Incremental Learning in vision-language models, combining Task Subspace Projection and Dynamic LoRA to reduce task confusion and balance adaptation.
AI.motivation: Pre-trained VLMs face catastrophic forgetting, zero-shot degradation, and new-task underfitting in Multi-Domain Task-Incremental Learning (MTIL), where existing cross-task identification (CTI) suffers from seen/unseen task confusion and adaptation modules lack adaptive parameter allocation.
AI.method: TSP-DLoRA introduces Task Subspace Projection (TSP) with a subspace-based task identifier classifier and feature projection for seen and unseen tasks, alongside Dynamic LoRA (DLoRA) that dynamically assigns LoRA modules across transformer layers based on task distributions.
AI.result: Experimental evaluations across 11 datasets using three performance metrics demonstrate the effectiveness of TSP-DLoRA for MTIL.
AI.conclusion: Subspace-based task identification and dynamic layer-wise LoRA allocation mitigate forgetting and task confusion in incremental VLM learning.

title: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
summary: Visual brain decoding translates neural activity into human-interpretable images. While recent EEG-to-image reconstruction methods rely on aligning EEG signals with pretrained visual embeddings to condition an image generator, we empirically demonstrate that stronger cross-modal alignment do not translate into comparable gains in reconstruction quality. This indicates that improving the input condition alone is insufficient; the generative process itself requires explicit supervision. Although Representation Alignment (REPA) offers a solution by guiding diffusion transformers with pretrained vision encoder features, we find that EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow these fixed targets. To address this mismatch, we introduce generation-derived supervision (GDS): an image-conditioned teacher that translates static image-encoder features into the internal representation space of a diffusion transformer. Our EEG-conditioned student generator closely tracks these dynamic targets during denoising, discarding the teacher at inference. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG, our approach consistently outperforms conditioning-centric baselines, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes generation-derived supervision (GDS) for EEG-to-image reconstruction, using an image-conditioned teacher to supervise an EEG-conditioned diffusion transformer and achieving state-of-the-art fidelity.
AI.motivation: Stronger cross-modal alignment between EEG signals and pretrained visual embeddings does not yield commensurate gains in image reconstruction, and EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow fixed vision-encoder targets in REPA.
AI.method: GDS trains an image-conditioned teacher to map static image-encoder features into the internal representation space of a diffusion transformer, providing dynamic denoising targets that an EEG-conditioned student generator tracks during training before discarding the teacher at inference.
AI.result: Evaluated on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG, GDS consistently outperforms conditioning-centric baselines and achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Supervising the internal denoising representations of the generator via an image-conditioned teacher is more effective than improving input-condition alignment alone for neural decoding.

title: GameWM: Toward Next-Generation Video Games with Interaction-Centric World Models
summary: For more than half a century, video games have pursued better graphics, more natural interaction, and more engaging gameplay. Generative video models (VMs) now bear on all three. Neural networks already draw most of the pixels in shipped games, and recent world models let a lightweight game engine keep the world state while a VM turns the engine's coarse proxy video into final frames. These systems, however, treat the VM as a renderer that only restyles motion the engine has already authored, which leaves most of its generative capacity unused and limits the diversity a game can offer. We present GameWM, a design for next-generation games built on a clear division of labor. The GameWM-engine keeps what must be exact: rules, state, camera, and the layout of the world, which also spares the video model from having to remember it. The GameWM-VM generates what is expensive to author by hand: the look of the world and the detail of the player's interactions. One game mechanic can then be realized in many visually and physically distinct ways, while its outcome stays exactly as the engine computed it. To realize this division of labor, we build GameWM as a complete system: a data engine centered on interactions rather than exploration, an interface through which authored character sheets, scene art, and skill descriptions enter the model, and a model family from 5B to 33B parameters with a real-time causal variant for play. Together they give every player a fresh version of the same game: each player's own character, world, and skills turn the same engine mechanics into a new experience, while every event keeps the timing and outcome the GameWM-engine computed.

AI.tldr: This paper presents GameWM, a game architecture pairing an exact game engine for rules and state with an interaction-centric generative video model (5B-33B) for visuals and player interactions.
AI.motivation: Existing world-model games use video models merely to restyle coarse proxy video from a game engine, leaving most generative capacity unused and limiting visual and physical diversity.
AI.method: GameWM divides labor between GameWM-engine (maintaining exact rules, state, camera, and layout) and GameWM-VM (5B to 33B parameters with a real-time causal variant), supported by an interaction-centric data engine and an interface for authored character sheets, scene art, and skill descriptions.
AI.result: GameWM realizes single game mechanics in diverse visual and physical ways while preserving exact engine timing and outcomes, enabling personalized characters, worlds, and skills in real-time play.
AI.conclusion: Separating deterministic game state from interaction-centric video generation unlocks diverse, customizable next-generation gameplay.

title: Size-Matched Nulls Reveal What Block Ablation Measures in MambaVision
summary: Hybrid vision backbones interleave Mamba state-space mixers with self-attention, and a block's role is usually probed by removing it and measuring the damage. We test what that measurement means in MambaVision. On all 50,000 ImageNet validation images and three model sizes, every block ablation is paired with a size-matched null, the same perturbation with its channels shuffled or their signs flipped. In top-1 accuracy and in true-class rank, real and null damage are nearly indistinguishable in absolute terms: pooled over the blocks of MambaVision-T, the content effect lies within [-0.044,+0.016] percentage points (90% interval). Two attention-only controls show that the test detects content, with real ablations worse than their nulls by up to 4.2 points in DeiT-Small and 1.0 point in Swin-T. Part of MambaVision's near-equivalence reflects how little damage its blocks do (0.11--0.34 points on average, against 1.7 and 2.1). Scaled by damage, its content share is comparable to Swin-T's in accuracy, lower in rank, and far below DeiT-Small's: single-block damage in MambaVision is small and mostly positional. Ablation also hides what blocks carry together: removing all blocks of one type compounds damage to 3.7--8.4 times the sum of single effects, far more than size-matched nulls, including nulls that keep the alignment between the blocks' perturbations; for adjacent pairs, aligned nulls reproduce most of it. Freezing input-dependent selection in all Mamba mixers shows that it accounts for 20--32% of the Mamba contribution, mainly through the B and C projections. We turn these results into a protocol for causal attribution in hybrid networks.

AI.tldr: This paper pairs block ablations in MambaVision with size-matched nulls across 50,000 ImageNet images, showing that single-block ablation damage is small and mostly positional rather than content-specific.
AI.motivation: Block ablation is widely used to probe hybrid Mamba-attention vision backbones, but it is unclear how much of the measured accuracy drop reflects learned block content versus perturbation size.
AI.method: Across three MambaVision sizes on ImageNet validation, the authors pair every block ablation with size-matched nulls (shuffled channels or flipped signs), compare against DeiT-Small and Swin-T controls, test multi-block group ablations, and freeze input-dependent selection in Mamba mixers.
AI.result: In MambaVision-T, real and null single-block damage are nearly indistinguishable (content effect within [-0.044, +0.016] percentage points), single blocks cause only 0.11-0.34 points of damage, removing all blocks of one type compounds damage 3.7-8.4x, and input-dependent selection accounts for 20-32% of the Mamba contribution.
AI.conclusion: Size-matched nulls reveal that single-block ablation underestimates content and misses multi-block interactions, motivating a more rigorous causal attribution protocol for hybrid networks.

title: dit.xpu : Taming DiT Sparse Inference on Mobile SoCs
summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) enable on-device image generation and editing but incur high attention costs at high resolutions. Existing sparse attention reduces computation, yet dynamic sparsity introduces preprocessing and irregular data accesses that poorly fit mobile NPUs. We present this http URL, a sparse DiT inference framework for heterogeneous mobile SoCs. this http URL combines tile-aligned sparse attention with anchor-based error compensation by exploiting slowly varying dense-sparse output residuals across denoising steps. Heterogeneous XPU collaboration overlaps NPU dense attention with GPU sparse calibration, while mask-guided dataflow reduces data transfers and layout conversion by overlapping data movement with computation. Across five DiT models on two Snapdragon smartphones, this http URL achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup over the Hexagon-NPU backend and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup over the fastest alternative, while preserving generation quality close to dense attention. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: This paper presents dit.xpu, a sparse DiT inference framework for heterogeneous mobile SoCs that achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup on Snapdragon smartphones.
AI.motivation: Diffusion Transformers incur high attention costs at high resolutions on mobile devices, and existing dynamic sparse attention introduces preprocessing and irregular memory accesses that perform poorly on mobile NPUs.
AI.method: dit.xpu combines tile-aligned sparse attention with anchor-based error compensation across denoising steps, overlaps NPU dense attention with GPU sparse calibration via heterogeneous XPU collaboration, and uses mask-guided dataflow to overlap data movement with computation.
AI.result: Across five DiT models on two Snapdragon smartphones, dit.xpu achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup over the Hexagon-NPU backend and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup over the fastest alternative while preserving generation quality.
AI.conclusion: Co-designing tile-aligned sparsity with heterogeneous NPU-GPU execution enables fast, high-quality DiT inference on mobile SoCs.

title: LC-ISP Benchmark: Learning Advanced ISP with Live and Capture Streams
summary: High-quality paired RAW-to-sRGB datasets are essential for data-driven ISP, yet existing datasets often rely on cross-device collection, causing misalignment and failing to faithfully reflect real capture conditions. We therefore introduce LC-ISP, a large-scale benchmark built from the intrinsic gap between a camera's live preview and offline capture streams. LC-ISP contains 53.9k spatially aligned groups, each comprising live RAW/live sRGB and multi-frame fused RGB/capture sRGB, and covers day, night, indoor, outdoor, and HDR scenes. It also provides capture-stream intermediates for modular supervision. We further develop a compact two-stage baseline that uses these intermediates as auxiliary targets. Under a 2.5-GFLOP budget for 448$\times$448 RAW inputs, it outperforms the strongest single-frame baseline by over 2 dB PSNR while improving texture, denoising, and color reproduction. LC-ISP supports realistic benchmarking, the design of supervision strategies, and the development of lightweight ISP models.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces LC-ISP, a 53.9k-group spatially aligned RAW-to-sRGB benchmark built from live preview and capture streams, and a compact two-stage baseline that improves PSNR by over 2 dB.
AI.motivation: Existing paired RAW-to-sRGB ISP datasets often rely on cross-device collection, which introduces spatial misalignment and fails to reflect real camera capture conditions.
AI.method: LC-ISP pairs live RAW/sRGB with multi-frame fused RGB/capture sRGB and capture-stream intermediates across 53.9k aligned groups spanning day, night, indoor, outdoor, and HDR scenes, and trains a compact two-stage baseline using intermediates as auxiliary targets.
AI.result: Under a 2.5-GFLOP budget for 448x448 RAW inputs, the proposed two-stage baseline outperforms the strongest single-frame baseline by over 2 dB PSNR while improving texture, denoising, and color reproduction.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting the intrinsic gap between live and capture streams yields well-aligned training data and auxiliary supervision for lightweight ISP models.

title: Generate, Align, and Restore: MLLM-Empowered Diffusion for Generalizable Low-light Image Enhancement
summary: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is essential to numerous vision applications operating under adverse illumination. Despite substantial advances, real-world nighttime enhancement remains challenging due to the scarcity of strictly aligned day-night pairs and complex degradations involving extreme darkness and heterogeneous artificial light sources, leading to fragile generalization. To overcome these challenges, we propose MrLIE (MLLM-empowered reference Low-light Image Enhancement), a novel reference-based unsupervised LLIE framework that synergizes the generative and reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with conditional diffusion. MrLIE employs the MLLM as a high-fidelity reference synthesizer and diagnostic critic, iteratively generating, diagnosing, and correcting normal-light references directly from degraded nighttime observations. Based on this, our method governs the enhancement process through two complementary mechanisms, in which a confidence offset module rectifies spatial-geometric inconsistencies for reference reliability and a structure-anchored injection scheme harmonizes aligned reference cues, low-light structural constraints, and ControlNet additive anchoring during the denoising process. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that MrLIE achieves superior perceptual quality, natural appearance, and robust generalization.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes MrLIE, an unsupervised low-light image enhancement framework that uses an MLLM as a reference synthesizer and critic to guide conditional diffusion, improving perceptual quality and generalization.
AI.motivation: Real-world nighttime image enhancement struggles with scarce aligned day-night pairs and complex degradations involving extreme darkness and heterogeneous artificial lighting.
AI.method: MrLIE uses an MLLM to iteratively generate, diagnose, and correct normal-light reference images from degraded inputs, then guides conditional diffusion via a confidence offset module for geometric alignment and a structure-anchored injection scheme with ControlNet anchoring.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that MrLIE achieves superior perceptual quality, natural appearance, and robust generalization compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Integrating MLLM-driven reference synthesis and critique with structure-anchored diffusion enables generalizable unsupervised low-light image enhancement.

title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Accepted manuscript of the article published in IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters (2026). \c{opyright} 2026 IEEE. Code: this https URL
summary: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The layer improves Pix2Pix by +0.060, +0.012, and +0.077 dB PSNR and by +0.0034, +0.0057, and +0.0135 SSIM, respectively (Wilcoxon p < 1e-6), and it improves CycleGAN and CUT on all three sets (+0.013 to +0.076 dB). It raises edge precision at the cost of edge recall (edge F1 -1.3% on the test set). On the latent diffusion model COP-GEN, it adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on the winter set, the only set with dual-polarization SAR. An ablation shows that the gate produces the gain for MC-dropout GANs, whose candidates are nearly identical, whereas verifier selection contributes up to +0.26 dB for diffusion, whose samples differ. The layer has zero trainable parameters and adds 0.4 ms per patch beyond the K=5 generator passes.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for SAR-to-optical translation that ranks stochastic candidates and gates high-frequency details, improving PSNR and SSIM across GANs and diffusion models.
AI.motivation: SAR-to-optical translators often hallucinate details unsupported by radar measurements, and standard pixel metrics fail to detect these structural hallucinations.
AI.method: SAR-TopoGuard draws K stochastic candidates, ranks them with a speckle-aware verifier using gradient-magnitude correlation with SAR and a hallucination-frequency index, and applies a SAR-guided frequency gate to admit high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it, adding 0.4 ms per patch.
AI.result: Across SEN1-2 and SEN12MS sets, SAR-TopoGuard improves Pix2Pix by +0.012 to +0.077 dB PSNR and +0.0034 to +0.0135 SSIM, improves CycleGAN and CUT on all sets, and adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on COP-GEN, with the gate driving GAN gains and verifier selection driving diffusion gains.
AI.conclusion: Training-free topological verification and frequency gating reduce hallucinations and improve structural fidelity in SAR-to-optical translation.

title: Unlocking Fine-Grained Cell Representations via Soft-Interior Rim Dense-Grid Pooling in Pathology Foundation Models
summary: Fine-grained cell representations are essential for characterizing cellular heterogeneity and tissue organization in computational pathology. Pathology foundation models (PFMs) provide powerful pretrained features for transferable tissue analysis. HoVer-Net uses task-trained segmentation and typing, whereas CellViT++ averages native-grid tokens assigned to detected nuclei. However, the former requires cell-specific training; the latter ignores fractional nuclear coverage and can mix nuclear content with neighbouring tissue. Therefore, we propose SRDP, short for Soft-interior Rim Dense-grid Pooling, a training-free geometry-aware readout. We apply the frozen patch projection at half stride, interleave four offset lattices, map the cell mask to fractional coverage weights, and concatenate whole-cell pooling with two inner boundary pools. Across four datasets and six frozen encoders, SRDP improves mean balanced accuracy by 5.68 percentage points over native token averaging across 24 settings, including 11.22 points on average for CoNIC and Lizard. SRDP converts a coarse frozen PFM lattice into a mask-aligned, fine-grained cell representation without updating the encoder.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Soft-interior Rim Dense-grid Pooling (SRDP), a training-free readout for frozen pathology foundation models that improves mean balanced cell classification accuracy by 5.68 percentage points.
AI.motivation: Averaging native-grid tokens in frozen pathology foundation models (PFMs) ignores fractional nuclear coverage and mixes nuclear features with neighboring tissue, whereas task-trained models require cell-specific supervision.
AI.method: SRDP applies the frozen patch projection at half stride, interleaves four offset lattices, weights tokens by fractional cell-mask coverage, and concatenates whole-cell pooling with two inner boundary pools.
AI.result: Across four datasets and six frozen encoders (24 settings), SRDP improves mean balanced accuracy by 5.68 percentage points over native token averaging, including an 11.22-point average gain on CoNIC and Lizard.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-aware dense-grid pooling extracts fine-grained, mask-aligned cell representations from coarse frozen PFMs without encoder retraining.

title: A Think Block Is Conditioning, Not a Plan
summary: Generative models increasingly write a chain of thought before drawing, and report large gains from doing so. We ask what that text contributes, by substitution rather than ablation: holding the generator, sampler and seeds fixed, we replace the think block with controlled alternatives and measure the image. Across a unified model with a think mode, a reinforcement-learned reasoning generator, and a planner driving a frozen diffusion model, the same picture emerges. Content-free prose of matched length is worth nothing or less ($-0.05$ to $-0.15$). One sentence from an unrelated 8B model, naming the subject and a few identifying details, matches the generator's own plan in three to six times fewer conditioning tokens. The value sits where the referent is in doubt: writing down a name is worth $+0.33$ when it is right and $+0.05$ when it is wrong, and where the generator already succeeds the whole effect is $-0.07 \pm 0.07$. Cutting a plan at the text encoder's window leaves 272 of 286 images byte-identical, and a plan rewritten to fit that window ties a bare identification ($+0.003 \pm 0.044$), so a plan contains nothing the identification does not already supply. Field-level interventions find only colour executed reliably, and a control writing the same sentences into the user prompt shows that limit belongs to the generator rather than to the planning channel. Two judges and two annotators replicate the central contrasts. A think block earns its keep as a specification of what to draw, not as a plan that is carried out.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates what chain-of-thought "think blocks" actually contribute to generative image models, finding that they function as conditioning specifications of what to draw rather than executable plans.
AI.motivation: Generative models increasingly use chain-of-thought reasoning before drawing and report large gains, but it is unclear whether the text acts as an executed plan or merely as conditioning.
AI.method: The authors perform controlled substitution experiments—holding the generator, sampler, and seeds fixed—across a unified think-mode model, a reinforcement-learned reasoning generator, and a planner driving a frozen diffusion model, replacing think blocks with content-free prose, single-sentence 8B-model identifications, truncated plans, and field-level interventions.
AI.result: Content-free prose yields -0.05 to -0.15, while a single sentence from an unrelated 8B model matches the generator's plan using 3 to 6 times fewer tokens; naming the referent adds +0.33 when right and +0.05 when wrong, cutting plans at the text encoder window leaves 272 of 286 images byte-identical, and field-level interventions show only colour is reliably executed.
AI.conclusion: A think block earns its keep as a specification of what to draw rather than a plan that is carried out.

title: RETR: A Structure-Preserving RGB-Event Transformer for Robust 3D Lane Detection
summary: Robust 3D lane detection requires accurate metric road geometry recovery from visual inputs, yet conventional RGB-based approaches suffer from fragile lane evidence under adverse illumination, motion blur, and long-range perspective compression. Event cameras offer complementary high-temporal-resolution, high dynamic-range structural cues that are robust to these challenges, but their sparse, motion-dependent responses cannot be directly fused into consistent 3D geometry. In this paper, we present the first attempt to introduce event cameras into 3D lane detection. To enable systematic research, we first build two multimodal benchmarks with metric 3D lane annotations: DSEC-3DLD (real-world sequences) and Ev-OpenLane (large-scale simulated sequences). We further propose RETR, a structure preserving transformer that converts complementary RGB and event observations into coherent 3D lane geometry. RETR first aligns modality consistent evidence through Reciprocal Context Flow Fusion, then preserves thin and uncertain lane structures with Uncertainty Aware Structural Consolidation, and finally decodes ordered lane hypotheses using a Geometry State Decoder with proposal conditioned initialization, reference conditioned query evolution, and diversified geometric inquiry. Extensive experiments show that RETR achieves state-of-the-art performance on both benchmarks, especially showing strong improvements in challenging lighting and complex road geometry scenarios. Code and dataset will be available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces event cameras into 3D lane detection by building two multimodal benchmarks (DSEC-3DLD and Ev-OpenLane) and proposing RETR, a structure-preserving RGB-Event transformer that achieves state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: Conventional RGB-based 3D lane detection suffers from fragile lane evidence under adverse illumination, motion blur, and long-range perspective compression, while sparse, motion-dependent event camera responses cannot be directly fused into consistent 3D geometry.
AI.method: The authors construct DSEC-3DLD (real-world) and Ev-OpenLane (simulated) benchmarks with metric 3D lane annotations, and propose RETR, which aligns modality-consistent evidence via Reciprocal Context Flow Fusion, preserves thin/uncertain structures via Uncertainty Aware Structural Consolidation, and decodes ordered lanes using a Geometry State Decoder.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that RETR achieves state-of-the-art performance on both DSEC-3DLD and Ev-OpenLane, with strong improvements in challenging lighting and complex road geometry scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Combining event cameras with structure-preserving transformer fusion and decoding enables robust metric 3D lane detection under adverse visual conditions.

title: AcousticBEV: Acoustic BEV Object Localization for Intelligent Vehicles
comment: Ziang Liu and Shiming Wang have equal contributions. Shiming Wang is the project lead
summary: Modern autonomous driving and driver assistance systems rely predominantly on cameras, radars and LiDARs for environmental perception. However, these modalities face different environmental limitations, including poor illumination for cameras and adverse weather for LiDAR. Acoustic sensing, particularly using microphone arrays, could provide complementary perception capabilities for autonomous driving, but has remained largely underexplored. In this work, we design a horizontally arranged microphone array that functions as the "ears" of a vehicle, enabling localization of nearby moving vehicles in a bird's-eye view (BEV) representation that captures both their relative direction and distance. Using this array, we collect a real-world driving dataset, AcousticScenes, which contains 2,117 static and 2,863 dynamic samples with synchronized spatial acoustic signals, LiDAR point clouds and 3D bounding box annotations. Building on this dataset, we propose AcousticBEV, a learning-based method for acoustic BEV object localization, which estimates the center locations of moving traffic participants in BEV from the microphone-array signals, conditioned on the ego vehicle's own speed. Experimental results demonstrate that AcousticBEV outperforms both classical signal-processing baselines and other learning-based methods, achieving F1 scores of $47.7 \pm 1.2$% on "Easy" scenarios and $45.1 \pm 1.4$% on "Difficult" cases. Our findings demonstrate that acoustic signals from a low-cost, vehicle-mounted microphone array can localize nearby moving vehicles in both azimuth and distance.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes AcousticBEV, a learning-based method for localizing nearby moving vehicles in bird's-eye view (BEV) using a vehicle-mounted microphone array, alongside a new real-world dataset AcousticScenes.
AI.motivation: Autonomous driving relies on cameras, radars, and LiDARs that face limitations in poor illumination or adverse weather, while complementary acoustic sensing using microphone arrays remains largely underexplored.
AI.method: The authors design a horizontally arranged microphone array, collect the AcousticScenes dataset (2,117 static and 2,863 dynamic samples with synchronized spatial audio, LiDAR, and 3D bounding boxes), and train AcousticBEV to estimate moving vehicle center locations in BEV from microphone-array signals conditioned on ego-vehicle speed.
AI.result: AcousticBEV outperforms classical signal-processing baselines and other learning-based methods, achieving F1 scores of 47.7 ± 1.2% on Easy scenarios and 45.1 ± 1.4% on Difficult cases.
AI.conclusion: Acoustic signals from a low-cost, vehicle-mounted microphone array can effectively localize nearby moving vehicles in both azimuth and distance.

title: Detecting Small Space Objects for Space Situational Awareness with Collaborative Edge AI
summary: With the rapid growth of space activities, near-Earth space is becoming increasingly congested, leading to a higher risk of spacecraft collisions and space debris generation. Recent close-proximity encounters and collision incidents necessitate efficient and cost-effective onboard systems for space object detection (SOD) and collision avoidance. While deep learning (DL) enabled Edge AI using low-cost vision sensors on single or multiple satellites has shown promises for SOD, significant challenges remain, including limited datasets, small SOD, and the lack of comprehensive performance assessments. This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview SOD and systematically benchmarks DL models and fusion strategies. Results show that higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD. For multiple views, image-level fusion reduces the combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion across the evaluated inter-satellite link (ISL) bandwidth. For larger view sets, feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better detection accuracy at the cost of analysis in the sensing-communication pipeline, revealing that multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded. Our work provides valuable design insights for future collaborative satellite network design, supporting the emerging space situational awareness and space traffic management requirements.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview space object detection (SOD) and systematically benchmarks deep learning models and fusion strategies under inter-satellite link (ISL) constraints.
AI.motivation: Near-Earth space congestion increases collision risks, requiring efficient onboard SOD, yet existing Edge AI approaches face limited datasets, small object sizes, and a lack of comprehensive performance assessments across single and multiple satellites.
AI.method: The authors benchmark deep learning models and compare image-level, feature-level, and attention-based fusion strategies for multiview collaborative SOD across evaluated ISL bandwidths.
AI.result: Higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD; image-level fusion reduces combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion, whereas feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better accuracy for larger view sets.
AI.conclusion: Multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded, providing design insights for collaborative satellite networks and space traffic management.

title: SplatFlow3D: Learning Scene Flow via 3D Motion Feature Splatting
summary: Considering the motion continuity and stability of 3D objects over short inter-frame intervals, introducing multi-frame settings in scene flow estimation can potentially address occlusion. In this paper, we propose a two-frame backbone, SimpleFlow3D, which integrates dense information from the image plane and sparse information from the depth dimension in a decoupling-followed-by-coupling manner by hierarchically constructing the 3D motion feature. SimpleFlow3D achieves SOTA results with minimal parameters. We also propose a weight-sharing multi-frame framework to splat the previous 3D motion feature to the current estimation process. The framework unifies the first and non-first frame inference by constructing pseudo inputs. After combining the proposed framework and backbone, the newly born multi-frame method SplatFlow3D further advances the state of the art. It achieves lower errors than the two-frame backbone, with fewer parameters than current methods. On both KITTI and Spring, SplatFlow3D ranked 1st over all published and submitted methods. Experiments show that SplatFlow3D improves occlusion handling, non-rigid motion estimation, and generalization to real-world scenes. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes SimpleFlow3D (a two-frame backbone) and SplatFlow3D (a weight-sharing multi-frame scene flow framework) that rank 1st on both KITTI and Spring with fewer parameters.
AI.motivation: Multi-frame scene flow estimation can address occlusion by leveraging motion continuity, but existing methods struggle to efficiently integrate dense image-plane and sparse depth information across frames with low parameter counts.
AI.method: SimpleFlow3D decouples and then couples dense image-plane and sparse depth information to hierarchically construct 3D motion features; SplatFlow3D extends this with a weight-sharing multi-frame framework that splats previous 3D motion features into the current estimation and unifies first and non-first frame inference via pseudo inputs.
AI.result: SplatFlow3D achieves lower errors than the two-frame backbone with fewer parameters than current methods, ranking 1st over all published and submitted methods on both KITTI and Spring while improving occlusion handling, non-rigid motion estimation, and real-world generalization.
AI.conclusion: Splatting 3D motion features across frames in a weight-sharing framework advances state-of-the-art scene flow estimation with high parameter efficiency.

title: Memorization Lives in a Few Attention Heads: Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models via Projection-Based Suppression
summary: Diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training samples during inference, raising serious privacy and copyright concerns. Existing inference-time mitigation methods often suppress conditional information globally, which may reduce memorization but can also harm semantic alignment and image quality. In this paper, we revisit memorization from the perspective of cross-attention heads. Through systematic analysis and targeted ablation, we find that memorization is mainly driven by a small subset of shallow-layer attention heads with abnormally strong semantic control, rather than by the entire cross-attention mechanism. Motivated by this finding, we propose Projection-based Top-k Attention Head Suppression, a targeted inference-time mitigation method. Our method first identifies the top-k attention heads most related to memorization using a semantic-control score, and then removes their condition-specific components through directional projection between conditional and unconditional representations. This design selectively weakens memorization-related features while preserving useful semantic information. Extensive experiments on different diffusion models and datasets show that our method effectively reduces memorization and achieves a better trade-off between memorization mitigation and image quality than existing approaches.

AI.tldr: The paper finds that memorization in diffusion models is driven by a small subset of shallow-layer cross-attention heads and proposes Projection-based Top-k Attention Head Suppression to mitigate it at inference time.
AI.motivation: Diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training samples, raising privacy and copyright concerns, while existing inference-time mitigations suppress conditional information globally and harm semantic alignment and image quality.
AI.method: The authors identify the top-k memorization-related cross-attention heads using a semantic-control score and remove their condition-specific components via directional projection between conditional and unconditional representations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across different diffusion models and datasets show that the method effectively reduces memorization and achieves a better trade-off between memorization mitigation and image quality than existing approaches.
AI.conclusion: Targeting specific shallow-layer cross-attention heads via directional projection mitigates diffusion memorization while preserving useful semantic information.

title: Few-Shot Visual Concept Extraction for Steering Diffusion Transformers
summary: Image steering aims to provide fine-grained control over concepts in generated images, enabling targeted and continuous manipulation without broadly altering the generation process. Recent steering methods for diffusion models primarily focus on the text-conditioning space or rely on costly auxiliary training. Deviating from that, we here propose a novel steering approach that extracts visual concept directions directly from the image-side activations of Diffusion Transformers. Specifically, we showcase few-shot concept extraction in the activation space using a simple difference-of-means estimator over intermediate residuals. We observe (a) scene-level concepts such as lighting, weather, and style are distributed across image tokens, as well as (b) local concepts such as object colors, textures, materials, and facial attributes are concentrated in specific regions. Towards controlling both concepts, we introduce a new unified training-free framework that uses global difference-of-means for (a) distributed concepts and masked difference-of-means for (b) local concepts, preventing local signals from being diluted by global averaging. Notably, using only a handful of positive and negative prompt pairs, our method identifies and extracts reusable concept directions that can be injected at inference for continuous steering. Quantitatively, our method outperforms text-encoder steering and training-free activation-editing baselines, as well as is competitive with specialized editing models. Our results suggest that as concept directions can be applied at patch level, our method enables precise targeted and compositional steering, manipulating multiple concepts in the same image.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a training-free framework that extracts visual concept directions directly from Diffusion Transformer image-side activations using few-shot global and masked difference-of-means estimators.
AI.motivation: Recent diffusion steering methods primarily operate in the text-conditioning space or require costly auxiliary training, limiting fine-grained, continuous, and compositional control over visual concepts.
AI.method: Observing that scene-level concepts are distributed across image tokens while local concepts are concentrated in specific regions, the authors use global difference-of-means for distributed concepts and masked difference-of-means for local concepts over intermediate residuals from a handful of positive and negative prompt pairs.
AI.result: Quantitatively, the method outperforms text-encoder steering and training-free activation-editing baselines, is competitive with specialized editing models, and enables patch-level targeted and compositional steering of multiple concepts.
AI.conclusion: Extracting reusable visual concept directions directly from Diffusion Transformer activations enables precise, training-free, and compositional image steering.

title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
summary: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean absolute error (MAE) on the other species, with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) below zero. The 423K-parameter student, 2.54 times smaller than its teacher, attains the lowest MAE (1.476 days) and highest within 1-day accuracy (56.1%) among 14 configurations, matching the best of six ImageNet-pretrained backbones (ConvNeXt-T, 1.503 days) at 66 times fewer parameters, 1.44ms per cube on a GPU and 5s re-adaptation. InvarOrd beats target-only training by 0.29 days (p = 0.031). Among alignment objectives, rank-invariant alignment retains the most ordinal structure (embedding rank correlation 0.183, QWK 0.112), whereas global discrepancy lowers the rank correlation to 0.049 and QWK to zero at only 0.014 days higher MAE.

AI.tldr: The paper presents InvarOrd, a three-stage framework for cross-species hyperspectral fish freshness assessment that adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes while preserving ordinal structure.
AI.motivation: Hyperspectral fish freshness models rarely transfer between species, labelling a new species is slow and destructive, and standard domain alignment can collapse the ordinal freshness axis.
AI.method: InvarOrd performs self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment via a rank-invariant shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact 423K-parameter student.
AI.result: On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), the 423K-parameter student (2.54x smaller than its teacher) achieves the lowest MAE (1.476 days) and highest within 1-day accuracy (56.1%) among 14 configurations, matching ConvNeXt-T (1.503 days) with 66x fewer parameters, 1.44 ms/cube GPU inference, 5 s re-adaptation, and beating target-only training by 0.29 days (p = 0.031).
AI.conclusion: Rank-invariant within-rank alignment and ordinal distillation enable label-efficient, fast cross-species hyperspectral freshness assessment without collapsing ordinal structure.

title: StyleJudge: A Human-Validated, In-Context-Learning Vision-Language Evaluator for Artistic Style Transfer
summary: Automatic evaluation of artistic style transfer remains an open problem: existing metrics score an image pair in isolation, without seeing an example of the intended style transformation, and correlate poorly with human judgment. We introduce StyleJudge, a compact vision-language evaluator conditioned on a small set of reference source-to-stylized pairs before scoring a query pair, mirroring how a human rater calibrates to a style before judging a candidate. On a human-annotated benchmark of 878 rated pairs across 12 artistic styles (728 from 10 training/validation styles, 150 from 2 unseen styles), our efficient 0.8B-parameter StyleJudge reaches a Pearson correlation of 0.291 (Spearman 0.325) with human ratings on seen styles and 0.381 on unseen ones. On seen styles, it achieves the highest positive correlation among tested metrics: Gram-matrix style loss and CLIP similarity correlate weakly ($r=0.041$, $r=0.168$), while LPIPS (scored higher when closer to the source) correlates negatively ($r=-0.404$). We achieve this by distilling evaluation knowledge from a 72B-parameter vision-language teacher used only during training, which reaches $r=0.327$, confirming that most of its human alignment survives compact distillation. For training, we build a dataset of source-to-stylized pairs across the 12 styles via LoRA-adapted diffusion, densified with graded intermediate examples from a high-resolution image-morphing pipeline so the evaluator recognizes partial and complete stylization. On two held-out validation styles, StyleJudge reaches 28.2% exact-match agreement with its teacher's structured scores versus 1.1% for the untuned base model, with 67.8% shorter reasoning traces, and scores a pair in 39 s (median) using 2.5 GB of GPU memory on one NVIDIA T4. We release the human-rating benchmark, annotation guideline, SDXL-adapted FreeMorph code, and model weights.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces StyleJudge, a 0.8B-parameter vision-language evaluator distilled from a 72B teacher that uses in-context reference pairs to score artistic style transfer with higher human correlation than existing metrics.
AI.motivation: Automatic evaluation of artistic style transfer scores image pairs in isolation without seeing examples of the intended style transformation and correlates poorly with human judgment.
AI.method: StyleJudge conditions on a small set of reference source-to-stylized pairs before scoring a query pair; it is distilled from a 72B vision-language teacher trained on LoRA-adapted diffusion pairs densified with graded intermediate morphing examples.
AI.result: On a human-annotated benchmark of 878 pairs across 12 styles, StyleJudge achieves Pearson r = 0.291 (Spearman 0.325) on seen styles and 0.381 on unseen styles, outperforming Gram-matrix loss (r = 0.041), CLIP (r = 0.168), and LPIPS (r = -0.404), while reaching 28.2% exact-match agreement with its teacher (vs. 1.1% untuned) in 39 s median time on a 2.5 GB T4 GPU.
AI.conclusion: Distilling in-context-learning evaluation from a large vision-language teacher into a compact 0.8B model provides human-aligned, resource-efficient assessment of artistic style transfer.

title: PALIN: Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR Multimodal 3D Object Detection with Benchmark
summary: 3D object detection is critical for intelligent transportation systems. LiDAR has been widely adopted for accurate geometric measurements; however, purely geometric representations remain ambiguous under sparse observations and occlusions, while cross-sensor multimodal fusion suffers from calibration and synchronization errors. To overcome these challenges, we leverage an Ouster LiDAR to construct PALIN (Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR), a large-scale intrinsically pixel-aligned multimodal dataset jointly capturing geometry and NIR intensity, comprising approximately 8,000 annotated frames from static urban intersections and diverse mobile suburban scenes. Building upon this dataset, we propose CMambaFusion, a novel fusion framework consisting of a four-directional Cross-Mamba module for bidirectional cross-modal interaction and a Gated Concat-Mamba module for joint feature refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PALIN enables effective multimodal learning, and CMambaFusion achieves superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over both LiDAR-only and representative fusion baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces PALIN, an 8,000-frame pixel-aligned LiDAR-NIR 3D object detection dataset, and proposes CMambaFusion, a Cross-Mamba and Gated Concat-Mamba multimodal fusion framework.
AI.motivation: Purely LiDAR-based 3D object detection is ambiguous under sparse observations and occlusions, while cross-sensor multimodal fusion often suffers from calibration and synchronization errors.
AI.method: The authors use an Ouster LiDAR to capture intrinsically pixel-aligned geometry and NIR intensity in PALIN (~8,000 annotated frames from urban intersections and suburban scenes), and propose CMambaFusion with a four-directional Cross-Mamba module and a Gated Concat-Mamba module.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that PALIN enables effective multimodal learning and CMambaFusion achieves superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over both LiDAR-only and representative fusion baselines.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsically pixel-aligned LiDAR-NIR sensing paired with Mamba-based cross-modal fusion provides an accurate and efficient solution for multimodal 3D object detection.

title: Beyond Paired Inputs: Learning to Leverage RGB-T Cross-Modal Relations in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) sensors provide complementary observations, yet their distinct sensing characteristics make effective cross-modal coordination challenging. Although existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can process paired RGB-T inputs, they often fail to translate cross-modal relations into effective task-specific decisions, leaving the potential of these relations to improve task performance and robustness largely untapped. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RelMLLM, an RGB-T MLLM that explicitly learns to exploit cross-modal relations in task-specific decision making. It represents modality reliability, the cross-modal relation, and the dominant modality as a verifiable decision state. We derive task-grounded supervision for this state by comparing RGB-only, TIR-only, and paired RGB-T task outcomes. A hierarchical relation-guided reward supervises modality-specific evidence, relation-state prediction, and the final task output, while encouraging consistency across evidence, relation, and decision. We evaluate RelMLLM on natural RGB-T grounding, RGB-T visual question answering, and held-out sensor degradation. RelMLLM improves grounding accuracy and degradation robustness over its Qwen3-VL baselines while preserving performance on general RGB-T reasoning benchmarks. These results demonstrate that effectively exploiting cross-modal relations leads to more accurate and robust RGB-T decisions. Code and model weights are publicly available.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes RelMLLM, an RGB-T multimodal large language model that explicitly models modality reliability, cross-modal relations, and dominant modality using a hierarchical relation-guided reward.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLMs can process paired RGB-T inputs but often fail to translate cross-modal relations into effective task-specific decisions, leaving performance and robustness gains untapped.
AI.method: RelMLLM represents modality reliability, cross-modal relation, and dominant modality as a verifiable decision state, deriving supervision by comparing RGB-only, TIR-only, and paired RGB-T outcomes with a hierarchical relation-guided reward.
AI.result: Evaluated on natural RGB-T grounding, RGB-T VQA, and held-out sensor degradation, RelMLLM improves grounding accuracy and degradation robustness over Qwen3-VL baselines while preserving general RGB-T reasoning performance.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly learning to exploit cross-modal relations leads to more accurate and robust RGB-T decision making in MLLMs.

title: Vegetation Health Classification for Low-Data and Edge Hardware Deployment
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with cameras are popular, viable tools for vegetation and environmental health monitoring. However, existing image classification methods are incompatible with UAV implementation for independent practitioners in remote, resource-constrained environments due to large dataset requirements, GPU hardware, inflexible retraining, and low interpretability. This paper presents a lightweight, interpretable vegetation classification algorithm operating with as few as five reference images per class, without GPUs or heavy machine learning frameworks. It uses a 2D hue-saturation histogram feature representation and Earth Mover's Distance or Quadratic Form Distance, paired with a log-likelihood probability score, to classify images into three vegetation health categories. We evaluated six systems: three custom pipelines and three established models across low-data scenarios ($n = 5, 10, 25$) and a full-data regime of 2,172 drone images from 28 South American locations. Our custom pipelines achieve competitive Top-1 accuracy (81--85\%) under low-data constraints, maintaining sub-1ms inference times that enable real-time classification and subsequently tasks such as seeding and watering. The algorithms also support incremental retraining without full model reconstruction. We validate edge feasibility by deploying the QFD variant on an ESP32 microcontroller, achieving 82.8\% accuracy with 1.01\% heap memory utilization (45kb), demonstrating that effective vegetation classification is achievable on low-cost, low-power embedded hardware without cellular connectivity.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a lightweight, interpretable vegetation health classification algorithm using 2D hue-saturation histograms and distance metrics that runs on an ESP32 microcontroller with as few as five reference images per class.
AI.motivation: Existing image classification methods for UAV vegetation monitoring require large datasets, GPU hardware, inflexible retraining, and offer low interpretability, making them incompatible with remote, resource-constrained deployment.
AI.method: The algorithm represents images as 2D hue-saturation histograms and uses Earth Mover's Distance or Quadratic Form Distance (QFD) paired with a log-likelihood probability score to classify three vegetation health categories, supporting incremental retraining.
AI.result: Across low-data regimes (n = 5, 10, 25) and 2,172 drone images from 28 South American locations, the custom pipelines achieve 81–85% Top-1 accuracy with sub-1 ms inference; deployed on an ESP32 microcontroller, the QFD variant achieves 82.8% accuracy using 45 KB (1.01%) heap memory.
AI.conclusion: Effective, real-time vegetation health classification is feasible on low-cost, low-power embedded hardware without GPUs or cellular connectivity.

title: DBHiCo: Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning for MRI Image Classification
summary: Automated Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) image classification provides a crucial non-invasive approach for neurological diagnosis, yet it is fundamentally challenged by inherent acquisition noise and high inter-subject structural similarity, which obscure subtle pathological variations, thereby limiting the performance of deep neural networks. While contrastive learning (CL) offers a promising mitigation strategy, existing paradigms rely on rigid binary partitions that ignore negative sample heterogeneity, and they fail to capture the cross-view structural consistency vital for fine-grained anatomical alignment. To address these barriers, we propose Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning (DBHiCo), a novel framework explicitly designed to collaboratively enforce structural consistency and semantic discrimination. Specifically, DBHiCo leverages a natural anatomical multi-view pair (original and skull-stripped MRI scans), processing them through a dual-branch architecture to seamlessly integrate holistic structural robustness with localized intracranial details. Crucially, we introduce a hierarchical contrastive loss that discards conventional binary constraints in favor of a margin-ranked similarity hierarchy. This mechanism explicitly orders positive and negative pairs based on their structural and semantic difficulty, thereby amplifying the fine-grained semantic discriminability of the learned representations. Extensive experiments across three diverse neurological datasets demonstrate that DBHiCo achieves state-of-the-art performance, consistently outperforming existing MRI multi-view representation learning and advanced contrastive fine-tuning methods.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes DBHiCo, a dual-branch hierarchical contrastive learning framework for MRI image classification that leverages original and skull-stripped scans with a margin-ranked similarity hierarchy.
AI.motivation: Automated MRI classification is challenged by acquisition noise and high inter-subject structural similarity, while existing contrastive learning methods rely on rigid binary partitions that ignore negative sample heterogeneity and cross-view structural consistency.
AI.method: DBHiCo processes natural anatomical multi-view pairs (original and skull-stripped MRI scans) through a dual-branch architecture and introduces a hierarchical contrastive loss that replaces binary constraints with a margin-ranked similarity hierarchy ordered by structural and semantic difficulty.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across three diverse neurological datasets show that DBHiCo achieves state-of-the-art performance, consistently outperforming existing MRI multi-view representation learning and contrastive fine-tuning methods.
AI.conclusion: Enforcing cross-view structural consistency and margin-ranked semantic discrimination improves fine-grained MRI representation learning for neurological diagnosis.

title: PathLoop: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Reasoning for Evidence-Grounded Whole-Slide Image Analysis
summary: Analyzing whole-slide images (WSIs) requires combining evidence across tissue regions and spatial scales. Multi-agent systems offer a promising approach to this task. However, existing systems make limited use of molecular evidence, often select visually prominent but less representative regions while overlooking global context, and struggle to reuse experience from previous cases. To address these challenges, we present PathLoop, a self-evolving multi-agent framework that integrates omics data for evidence-grounded WSI analysis. Specifically, PathLoop coordinates visual and omics interpreters across slide, patch, and pixel levels, using molecular signals to guide region selection and combining local tissue details with global slide features. A judgment agent then checks the consistency of the collected evidence against Pathology-Wiki, a knowledge base built from 48 entries across 24 organ systems, and triggers re-examination when the evidence is inconsistent. To reuse past experience, a four-level memory stores reasoning trajectories, practical tips, skills, and tools to guide future cases, forming a loop of evidence collection, review, and memory update. We evaluate PathLoop on four TCGA cohorts with biomarker prediction, survival prediction, and subtype classification. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of PathLoop across these tasks and support its use for evidence-grounded WSI analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper presents PathLoop, a self-evolving multi-agent framework for whole-slide image (WSI) analysis that integrates omics data, checks evidence against a pathology knowledge base, and reuses past experience via a four-level memory.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-agent systems for WSI analysis make limited use of molecular evidence, often select visually prominent but unrepresentative regions while missing global context, and struggle to reuse experience from previous cases.
AI.method: PathLoop coordinates visual and omics interpreters across slide, patch, and pixel levels using molecular signals to guide region selection; a judgment agent verifies evidence consistency against Pathology-Wiki (48 entries across 24 organ systems) and triggers re-examination if needed, while a four-level memory stores trajectories, tips, skills, and tools.
AI.result: Evaluations on four TCGA cohorts for biomarker prediction, survival prediction, and subtype classification demonstrate PathLoop's effectiveness across all tasks.
AI.conclusion: Integrating omics-guided region selection, knowledge-base consistency checking, and experience memory enables more reliable, evidence-grounded WSI analysis.

title: Lesion-Aware Explainable AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading from Fundus Images
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 9 tables. Truong Thinh Nguyen and Hai Phong Nguyen contributed equally. Corresponding author: Truong Thinh Nguyen
summary: Post-hoc explanations of deep-learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are difficult to trust because different attribution methods highlight different retinal regions for the same image, and a visually plausible heatmap does not show that the highlighted pixels drive the prediction. We propose the Consensus-Calibrated Explanation Map (CCEM), which fuses Grad-CAM++, Ada-SISE, and SmoothGrad Integrated Gradients (SG-IG) using image-specific weights derived from annotation-free reliability cues: deletion sensitivity, inter-method agreement, compactness, retinal containment, and peak structure. CCEM explains a frozen ordinal grader, an EfficientNet-B7 with CBAM and a scalar regression head, pre-trained on EyePACS 2015 in Stage 1 and fine-tuned on APTOS 2019 in Stage 2 with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK)-optimized thresholds; it reaches a QWK of 0.920 on the hidden Kaggle test set and 0.559 on the external MAPLES-DR cohort. Explanations are evaluated on MAPLES-DR, 198 MESSIDOR images with expert pixel-level lesion annotations that are never used for training, threshold fitting, or fusion. On the 193 images with annotated lesions, CCEM obtains the highest Soft Pointing Game score (69.61%; 95% CI 63.7-75.3), defined as the ratio of the strongest lesion-supported saliency to the global map maximum rather than a lesion detection rate, together with the lowest deletion AUC (0.570) and the best deletion-insertion balance (0.115); each gain is significant against the strongest single explainer on paired tests. Annotation-free, per-image reliability weighting therefore turns three disagreeing explainers into one map whose peak evidence is more lesion-supported and more faithful to the model than that of any single explainer.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Consensus-Calibrated Explanation Map (CCEM), which fuses three attribution methods using annotation-free per-image reliability cues to produce more lesion-supported and faithful explanations for diabetic retinopathy grading.
AI.motivation: Post-hoc explanations for diabetic retinopathy grading are hard to trust because different attribution methods highlight different retinal regions and visually plausible heatmaps may not drive the prediction.
AI.method: CCEM fuses Grad-CAM++, Ada-SISE, and SmoothGrad Integrated Gradients using image-specific weights derived from annotation-free reliability cues (deletion sensitivity, inter-method agreement, compactness, retinal containment, and peak structure) to explain a frozen EfficientNet-B7+CBAM ordinal grader.
AI.result: The grader achieves 0.920 QWK on Kaggle and 0.559 on MAPLES-DR; on 193 MESSIDOR images with annotated lesions, CCEM achieves the highest Soft Pointing Game score (69.61%, 95% CI 63.7–75.3), lowest deletion AUC (0.570), and best deletion-insertion balance (0.115), significantly outperforming the strongest single explainer.
AI.conclusion: Annotation-free, per-image reliability weighting turns disagreeing explainers into a single map that is more lesion-supported and faithful to the model.

title: Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
summary: The multi-level tiled map service is widely used and serves as a kind of digital infrastructure. These map tiles are usually rendered from vector data, whose update needs to walk or drive with professional equipment to check every points of interest. This leads to inconvenience and expensive cost in timely updating maps. Compared with vector data, aerial images are much easier and cheaper to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-level map generation framework that can automatically generate accurate and consistent maps with multiple zoom levels from aerial images. It consists of a level-aware map generator and a consistency-aware map generator. The level-aware map generator is able to generate accurate initial maps with realistic details for each zoom level. The consistency-aware map generator regards initial maps at each zoom level as a sequence and builds the connection between them, so as to guarantee content consistency between maps at different zoom levels. Furthermore, we collect a large-scale high-quality dataset called Multi-Level Map (MLM) for map generation at multiple zoom levels. Experiments on our MLM dataset show that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art map generation methods on both comprehensive quantitative metrics and perceptual quality.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a multi-level map generation framework that automatically generates consistent maps across multiple zoom levels from aerial images, along with a new Multi-Level Map (MLM) dataset.
AI.motivation: Multi-level tiled map services are typically rendered from vector data that is expensive and inconvenient to update manually, whereas aerial images are much cheaper and easier to obtain.
AI.method: The framework combines a level-aware map generator to produce accurate initial maps with realistic details at each zoom level, and a consistency-aware map generator that treats the initial maps as a sequence to enforce cross-zoom content consistency.
AI.result: Experiments on the newly collected Multi-Level Map (MLM) dataset show that the proposed method outperforms previous state-of-the-art map generation methods on both quantitative metrics and perceptual quality.
AI.conclusion: Modeling multi-zoom map generation as a sequence-consistent synthesis task enables accurate, low-cost map updates directly from aerial imagery.

title: EndoComparer: Comparative Surgical Video Question Answering with Pseudo-Siamese Visual Adaptation and Perceive-then-Compare Reasoning
summary: Purpose: Surgical training benefits from explicit comparison between cases: in patient condition, in technique and in skill proficiency. Surgical vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising and flexible interface for this purpose. Yet current VLMs typically see one video at a time, and they often fall short when asked to compare videos. Methods: We propose EndoComparer, a VLM for comparative surgical video question answering with two components. (a) A Pseudo-Siamese Visual LoRA (PSVL) gives each video slot its own low-rank adapter over a shared frozen vision encoder, separating the two videos in the visual pathway at the cost of a single encoder pass. (b) A Perceive-then-Compare chain of thought (PtC-CoT) trains the model to first state what each video shows, then derive the answer from these statements. We further curate EndoDiffVQA, a benchmark of nearly 11K multiple-choice questions on video-pair over cholecystectomy and gastric bypass procedures, covering anatomy, tool, action and skill. Results: EndoComparer outperforms strong generalist and surgical VLMs on detecting and specifying difference between videos. Ablations show that two proposed components contribute complimentarily, and the model remains more robust under a video-swap control that exposes confusion between the two videos. Conclusion: Providing a dedicated visual reasoning path through PSVL and PtC-CoT makes cross-case comparison of surgical videos more robust for VLMs. EndoDiffVQA and EndoComparer provide a benchmark and a strong baseline for this task. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: The paper introduces EndoComparer, a vision-language model for comparative surgical video QA, and EndoDiffVQA, a benchmark of nearly 11K multiple-choice questions on surgical video pairs.
AI.motivation: Surgical training benefits from explicit case-to-case comparison, yet current vision-language models typically process one video at a time and struggle when asked to compare two videos.
AI.method: EndoComparer pairs a Pseudo-Siamese Visual LoRA (PSVL), which gives each video slot its own low-rank adapter over a shared frozen vision encoder, with a Perceive-then-Compare chain of thought (PtC-CoT) that states what each video shows before deriving the answer; the authors also curate EndoDiffVQA over cholecystectomy and gastric bypass procedures.
AI.result: EndoComparer outperforms strong generalist and surgical VLMs on detecting and specifying differences between videos, with ablations confirming complementary gains from PSVL and PtC-CoT and improved robustness under a video-swap control.
AI.conclusion: Dedicated dual-path visual adaptation and perceive-then-compare reasoning make cross-case surgical video comparison substantially more robust for VLMs.

title: Learning Spatially Aware Audio-Visual Features from Videos with Mono Audio
summary: Comprehensive audio-visual perception requires both semantic and spatial reasoning. Existing spatial models suffer from poor generalization due to data scarcity, while semantic-only models fail to capture spatial characteristics completely. We introduce a model capable of jointly reasoning over binaural audio and vision on semantic and spatial tasks with improved generalization. To overcome the shortage in real-world data, we develop an automatic pipeline that localizes the sound source in a video, estimates its relative 3D trajectory, and renders binaural audio. We then use this to spatialize VGGSound, allowing us to train at a much larger scale. We demonstrate improved performance and generalization on spatial reasoning tasks while still remaining competitive on semantic tasks compared to semantic-only models.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a model that jointly reasons over binaural audio and vision for semantic and spatial tasks, trained at scale by automatically spatializing VGGSound videos from mono audio.
AI.motivation: Comprehensive audio-visual perception requires both semantic and spatial reasoning, but existing spatial models generalize poorly due to data scarcity while semantic-only models fail to capture spatial cues.
AI.method: The authors build an automatic pipeline that localizes the sound source in a video, estimates its relative 3D trajectory, and renders binaural audio, using it to spatialize VGGSound for large-scale joint audio-visual training.
AI.result: The trained model demonstrates improved performance and generalization on spatial reasoning tasks while remaining competitive with semantic-only models on semantic tasks.
AI.conclusion: Automatically spatializing large-scale mono-audio video datasets enables joint spatial and semantic audio-visual representation learning with strong generalization.

title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
summary: Effective planning requires representations that preserve task-relevant geometry and object identity while ignoring visual variation that does not alter the task. Existing evaluations of visual generalization often change several factors simultaneously, making the source of a failure difficult to identify. We introduce a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses. Training and evaluation houses share floor plans, object locations, goals, and start states, while visual factors are changed individually or in combination. Across model-free reinforcement learning (RL), model-based RL, and agents using frozen pretrained visual representations, our results show that appearance changes impair navigation, but their effects differ sharply by factor. Surface material changes account for most of the average change in success, whereas clutter and lighting have little effect. The magnitude of a global image statistics shift does not reliably predict performance: changing only the goal object's appearance can substantially impair an end-to-end agent despite a small image-level change. We found that a model based agent that plans over frozen features from the pretrained DINOv2 image encoder achieves the highest success (0.83) under the full shift, but remains sensitive to surface appearance.
